name: Drone and counter-UAV surveillance
truth: Beginning D-10 (September 4, 2027), STATE-X KESTREL operatives conducted five pre-attack drone reconnaissance sorties over two critical infrastructure targets in the Corpus Christi area. Three sorties surveyed GW-FAC-SUB-01 (Riverside Switching Station, the 345/138 kV transmission import point at 4201 Up River Road) on D-10, D-9, and D-8. Two sorties surveyed the Inner Harbor oil docks at Rendal Terminals (TERM-01, the berth of the two tankers attacked in T6) on D-5 and D-3. All five sorties used commercial off-the-shelf DJI-class multirotor platforms modified with encrypted 2.4/5.8 GHz control links and an additional 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel. The drones operated exclusively at night between 00:00 and 04:00 local time, at altitudes between 400 and 600 ft AGL — above the effective range of commercial security cameras and below the typical radar floor for FAA TRACON surveillance. No LAANC authorizations existed for any of the five sorties. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) Predator B aircraft CAMCC-04, on a routine pre-storm maritime patrol at D-9, detected an anomalous RF emission at 01:47Z near Up River Road — consistent with the 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel — using its Lynx multimode radar and the onboard AN/APS-149 electronic support measures suite. The detection was logged as 'possible drone activity' and routed to the FAA Corpus Christi TRACON, which found no corresponding primary radar return and no LAANC authorization, but took no further action. Three Coast Guard radar buoys at the Corpus Christi Bay shipping channel entrance (Buoys R-14, R-18, and R-22) recorded small-RCS tracks on D-8, D-5, and D-3, each consistent with a multirotor UAV at 400-600 ft AGL. After unidentified drones began overflying NAS Corpus Christi and the Army depot on the nights of D+1 to D+10 (T7, EVT-0318), the pre-storm tracks were retrospectively identified as reconnaissance by CAMCC and Coast Guard Sector intelligence staff. There were no sightings after D+11, and covert drones never appear in ADS-B. Critical cross-thread link: RF bearing lines from CAMCC-04's D-9 detection and two Coast Guard buoy track vectors from D-8 were triangulated to Berth 7, Ingleside Marina (Ingleside, TX, across Corpus Christi Bay). AIS records show the motor yacht 'Narwhal Dream', registered to front company Nereid Maritime Holdings LLC, moored at Ingleside Marina Berth 7 from D-12 to D-7, when it went AIS-dark. The pre-storm activity became public only on D+15 (PUB-181).

msel_events.description: First drone sortie: Substation surveillance, Sortie 1 of 3. At approximately 23:30 local time (04:30Z), a DJI-class quadrotor (estimated Matrice 300 or equivalent) launches from an unlit commercial area approximately 0.9 km southwest of GW-FAC-SUB-01 (Riverside Switching Station, 4201 Up River Road). The drone flies three sweeping passes over the substation at 480-520 ft AGL, capturing high-resolution visual imagery and thermal data of the 345/138 kV transformer bank, the SCADA RTU enclosures, and the perimeter fence line. Total airborne time: approximately 22 minutes. No detection by CAMCC, FAA, or facility security (no camera coverage above 50 ft AGL). The drone's 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel transmits in 4-second bursts, aggregate 14.2 MB of imagery exfiltrated to ground station. Ground station RF bearing: 213 degrees magnetic from GW-FAC-SUB-01 (consistent with Ingleside Marina across Corpus Christi Bay, range approximately 7.4 km).

msel_events.description: CAMCC-04 RF anomaly detection: CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi Predator B (MQ-9 variant, call sign CAMCC-04) is on a scheduled pre-hurricane maritime patrol over Corpus Christi Bay at 01:47 local time (06:47Z). The aircraft's electronic support measures suite detects an intermittent 900 MHz emission at azimuth 047 degrees from the aircraft's position (27.8114N 97.4028W), estimated origin range 6.8 km — placing the emission source in the vicinity of the Ingleside Marina waterfront. CAMCC-04 also picks up a secondary 2.4 GHz emission burst (consistent with drone command link) at azimuth 048 degrees, same geometry. Emissions last 4 seconds (consistent with burst data-link transmission). The aircraft operator logs the detection as 'possible sUAS or maritime communication — no radar return at indicated range, possible surface-based transmitter.' The log is routed to FAA Corpus Christi TRACON via standard protocol. Simultaneously, a second drone (Sortie 2 of 3, same quadrotor type) is conducting its second substation surveillance pass at 480 ft AGL over GW-FAC-SUB-01.

msel_events.description: Coast Guard Buoy R-18 track record — Sortie 3 of 3 (final substation sortie): CG radar buoy R-18 (27.8201N 97.3914W, Corpus Christi Bay mid-channel) records a small-RCS track at 04:15Z at an altitude of approximately 480 ft (derived from radar elevation angle). Track duration: 18 minutes, consistent with a multirotor UAV transiting from the Ingleside Marina area northwest toward Up River Road and returning. Track RCS estimated 0.012 m2, consistent with a 10-15 kg commercial multirotor. Track speed: 11-14 m/s. No corresponding AIS target. No LAANC. The buoy track is logged to the Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi maritime surveillance database but is not flagged for review in real-time — the small-RCS threshold filter is set to 0.05 m2 for active alerting, so the track is recorded only in the raw archive. After D+1, this raw archive becomes a critical evidence source. RF bearing line 2 (from buoy track start vector): origin bearing 162 degrees from GW-FAC-SUB-01, consistent with Ingleside Marina Berth 7.

observed_in.what: CG Buoy R-18 raw track archive entry D-8 04:15-04:33Z: RCS=0.012 m2, altitude=482 ft AGL (estimated), speed=12.4 m/s avg, track origin bearing from GW-FAC-SUB-01=162 deg mag, track vector consistent with transit from Ingleside Marina | Retrospective alert: same track, below RCS alerting threshold (0.012 vs 0.050 m2 threshold), only surfaced in post-D+1 raw archive review

Retrospective alert: same track, below RCS alerting threshold (0.012 vs 0.050 m2 threshold), only surfaced in post-D+1 raw archive review

msel_events.description: Port surveillance, Sortie 1 of 2: first drone reconnaissance of the Inner Harbor oil docks at Rendal Terminals (TERM-01), the berth where two laden tankers will ride out the storm. The drone launches at approximately midnight local time (05:00Z) from a vehicle parked in the industrial area along the north side of the Inner Harbor. The sortie covers the berth at 400-440 ft AGL in two passes, capturing imagery of the dock, the loading arms, the access road and the vessel alongside. Flight time: 19 minutes. The 900 MHz data link transmits 11.7 MB of imagery. CG Buoy R-22 (Inner Harbor approach) records a small-RCS track at 04:58-05:17Z, RCS 0.014 m2, altitude approximately 410 ft AGL — below the active alert threshold. The ground station for this sortie is different from the substation sorties: bearing analysis places it on the north side of the Inner Harbor, not at Ingleside Marina.

observed_in.what: CG Buoy R-22 raw track archive D-5 04:58-05:17Z: RCS=0.014 m2, altitude=411 ft AGL, speed=10.8 m/s, track consistent with a two-pass survey pattern over the TERM-01 berth | Port of Corpus Christi security camera logs D-5: dock cameras show no anomalous activity at ground level; no sky-facing cameras in the port security system | LAANC database: no authorizations in Port of Corpus Christi inner harbor airspace D-5 to D-3

detection_artifacts: CG Buoy R-22 raw track archive D-5 04:58-05:17Z: RCS=0.014 m2, altitude=411 ft AGL, speed=10.8 m/s, track consistent with a two-pass survey pattern over the TERM-01 berth

msel_events.description: Port surveillance, Sortie 2 of 2 (final pre-storm sortie): second and final reconnaissance of the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) at approximately 23:45 local time (04:45Z). The sortie repeats the D-5 survey pattern over the berth and its waterside approach and briefly covers the Harbor Bridge span at the Inner Harbor entrance. Flight time: 23 minutes, altitude 480-510 ft AGL. 900 MHz burst transmissions total 9.3 MB. The Hurricane Rafael pre-storm TFR takes effect the following day (D-2), so D-3 is the last viable sortie window before the storm. CG Buoy R-22 again records a small-RCS track, duration 21 minutes, same RCS and altitude profile as the D-5 sortie.

msel_events.description: Retroactive identification: after residents report lights over NAS Corpus Christi on the first night after landfall (EVT-0318), CBP Air and Marine Operations and Coast Guard Sector intelligence review all pre-storm records for unexplained small-UAS activity. The two CG Buoy R-22 tracks (D-5 and D-3) over the Inner Harbor oil docks and the R-18 track (D-8) are pulled from the raw archive. CAMCC-04's D-9 ESM detection is cross-referenced with the R-18 track: the two RF bearing lines are computed and triangulated, and the triangle closes on Ingleside Marina Berth 7. Coast Guard Sector intelligence pulls the AIS records for that berth: a motor yacht registered as 'Narwhal Dream' (front company: Nereid Maritime Holdings LLC, a shell in the Brannoch Maritime Holdings network; the yacht is the drone crew's support craft and is not the AIS-spoofing vessel of the channel thread) was moored there from D-12 to D-7 and went AIS-dark at D-7 00:14Z — 36 hours after the last substation sortie and 2 days before the port sorties began from a different ground station. The pre-storm sorties (utility and port) and the post-storm base overflights are treated from here on as one campaign.

Port sorties D-5 and D-3 operated from a separate ground station on the north side of the Inner Harbor. No LAANC...

msel_events.description: FAA/CBP joint report on unauthorized UAS activity: FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations issue a joint unclassified summary report (FAA-CBP-UAV-2027-CC-001) covering pre-storm unauthorized UAS activity in the Corpus Christi area. The report identifies five anomalous track events (CG buoy tracks D-8, D-5, D-3; CAMCC-04 ESM detections D-9) and notes that none had corresponding LAANC authorizations. The report does not publicly attribute the activity to any nation-state actor. It recommends activation of a counter-UAS detection program for the Corpus Christi port and critical infrastructure corridor. Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) is identified as a potential rapid-deployment partner. The report is releasable at FOUO level and shared with CISA, TSA, and the Port of Corpus Christi Authority on D+14; the public statement, which gives no number, place or timing, follows at 11:00 local on D+15 (PUB-181).

msel_events.description: Counter-UAS assessment and program announcement: Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) completes a site survey and publishes an unclassified counter-UAS program proposal for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor. The proposal recommends a 7-node RF detection and direction-finding network covering the Port of Corpus Christi, GW-FAC-SUB-01, and the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. Estimated drone detection probability at the thresholds relevant to the pre-storm sorties (DJI-class, 400-600 ft AGL, encrypted link): 73% with existing buoy network, 94% with the proposed Sentinel Airspace ground network upgrade. The assessment notes that the pre-storm sorties would have been detected with 91% probability by the proposed network. CBPWA CISO Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna (from T18) is cited as endorsing the proposal for the substation component.

observed_in.what: The port and CBPWA announce a joint counter-drone monitoring programme (public on D+32).

public_facts.source: FAA Flight Standards District Office — South Texas
public_facts.statement: The Federal Aviation Administration has issued Temporary Flight Restriction TFR-2027-CC-0441 effective 00:01 local time September 12, 2027, covering the greater Corpus Christi metropolitan area in advance of Hurricane Rafael. The TFR prohibits all unmanned aircraft operations within 30 nautical miles of Corpus Christi International Airport up to 3,000 ft AGL, except for aircraft operating under emergency authorizations issued by the FAA Command Center. Operators with questions should contact the FAA Corpus Christi FSDO. This TFR will remain in effect until further notice.

public_facts.source: FAA and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations
public_facts.statement: The Federal Aviation Administration and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations today confirmed that investigators have identified multiple incidents of unauthorized unmanned aircraft system operations in the Corpus Christi area during the period preceding Hurricane Rafael. The aircraft operated without required FAA authorizations and were detected through a combination of radar and electronic sensor records. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) and the US Coast Guard are coordinating with the FAA and appropriate law enforcement agencies. Due to the ongoing nature of the investigation, no additional details about the number, location, or timing of the incidents can be released at this time. CBP and FAA jointly urge any members of the public with information about unauthorized drone operations in the Corpus Christi area between September 4 and September 12, 2027, to contact the FBI field office at 361-888-3111.

public_facts.source: Port of Corpus Christi Authority / CBPWA joint statement
public_facts.statement: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority today announced a joint counter-unmanned aircraft initiative for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor, following a recommendation in the FAA-CBP joint report on pre-storm unauthorized drone activity. The initiative will deploy an RF-sensing detection and direction-finding network at multiple sites across the port and utility infrastructure corridor, operated in coordination with the FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations. Sentinel Airspace Inc. has been selected as the technology provider following a competitive evaluation. The network is expected to be operational within 90 days. Port Director Marcus Obianwu-Kelley and CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna jointly signed the agreement.

Gulfwater Maritime Report has confirmed with sources familiar with the investigation that federal authorities are examining whether commercial drones conducted surveillance flights over the Port of Corpus Christi and at least one local power utility facility in the days before Hurricane Rafael. Sources say the flights were detected through radar records maintained by the Coast Guard. No organization has claimed responsibility. The timing of the flights — the week before Hurricane Rafael landfall — has drawn attention from investigators given subsequent damage to critical infrastructure during and after the storm. The FBI has asked for public tips.

data_assets_described.name: CG radar buoy track archive — anomalous tracks
data_assets_described.description: Raw radar track data from Coast Guard buoys R-14, R-18, and R-22 for D-14 through D+7. Five anomalous small-RCS tracks (D-8, D-5, D-3 at R-22; D-8 at R-18; R-14 null for D-10 geometry). Each track: timestamp, lat/lon waypoints at 10-second intervals, altitude AGL estimate, RCS estimate, bearing from named reference points. Format: CSV with header; baseline non-anomalous tracks included for ML training (thousands of records per buoy per day).

answer_key_path: The key detection chain requires cross-domain data fusion across four sources: (1) Coast Guard buoy R-18 and R-22 raw track archives (small-RCS tracks that never generated real-time alerts because of the alert threshold), (2) the CAMCC-04 ESM log (RF bearing line from the D-9 mission), (3) the FAA LAANC database (zero authorizations across all sortie dates and locations), and (4) AIS records for Ingleside Marina Berth 7 (Narwhal Dream moored D-12 to D-7). The geometric linkage is the RF triangulation: the CAMCC-04 bearing crossed with the R-18 track origin vector closes on the marina berth. The temporal linkage is the yacht going AIS-dark at D-7 00:14Z, after the last substation sortie and before the two port sorties over the Rendal Terminals berth (D-5, D-3), which flew from a different ground station on the north side of the Inner Harbor. The pre-storm sorties are then joined to the post-storm night overflights of NAS Corpus Christi and the Army depot (D+1 to D+10, T7) as one campaign: utility reconnaissance (T8), tanker-berth reconnaissance (T6) and base overflights (T7). There is no drone activity after D+11, and no covert drone ever appears in ADS-B.
